tweets.text:
This.

Also, on top of the VERY fast diagnosis and root-cause analysis, it can and will suggest a solution to fix this, based on real code for similar problems it has learned from in the ingested training data.

Not the panicked dev at 3am trying to "prevent this in the future".
Someone replied to a webhook I sent with a 584 HTTP error status, and I really don't know what to do with that 🤣
„You only need 800 customers at $20 or something something“
Is there a prediction market on whether Anthropic will do a "well, actually, Fable will stay on the Max plan" tomorrow?

This is a surprisingly resonant perspective. Any game I ever played that had a cheat mode became completely irrelevant once cheats were applied. The intrinsic challenge of constantly charging at the boundaries of the game made it worth my time.

Similar with coding. And careful here: I'm not talking about the act of building a software product. I'm purely looking at the act of writing code for a machine to eventually execute.

The moment agentic systems came into play, my personal focus shifted from "is this good code" to "can I create the surrounding framework for any machine-generated code to run reliably?"

The act of writing code got completely devalued. There is no joy in writing code when agentic systems write more than I ever could. I immediately fled into a "management role", orchestrating and optimizing the working environment of my agents. 

What a ridiculous time to be alive.
